encounters.cc: Bilateral knee pain and stiffness developing gradually over 6 weeks, worse with stairs and prolonged sitting; patient seeks counseling on reducing long-term joint damage risk.

lines: Bilateral knee pain and stiffness developing gradually over 6 weeks, worse with stairs and prolonged sitting; patient seeks counseling on reducing long-term joint damage risk.
She describes aching in both knees, especially after a long day of teaching, and notes that the pain is worse when going up or down stairs.
The stiffness tends to occur after prolonged sitting and improves somewhat with movement.
She reports no redness, warmth, or swelling in the joints.
She admits to minimal exercise lately but had recently attempted to rejoin a weekend hiking group.
After a few hikes, she found that her knee pain significantly worsened, which discouraged her from continuing.
She has no morning stiffness, no involvement of her hands or other joints,
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
Her mother underwent knee replacement surgery in her 60s.
Over the past year, she has gained about 9 kg (20 lb) due to emotional eating after her father’s passing.
She smokes about half a pack of cigarettes daily and has done so for nearly two decades.
Her diet is irregular, and she often eats takeout or processed foods.
On exam, her height is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) and weight is 91 kg (200 lb), giving her a BMI of 32.2 kg/m².
Knee examination shows full range of motion, no effusion, and mild crepitus during flexion and extension.
No tenderness is present over the joint lines or ligaments, and there is no erythema.
Strength, sensation, and reflexes are intact in both lower extremities.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of intermittent burning retrosternal chest pain occurring after meals and lasting hours, with sensation of food sticking; denies exertional component.

lines: Six-month history of intermittent burning retrosternal chest pain occurring after meals and lasting hours, with sensation of food sticking; denies exertional component.

She presents to the Cardiology clinic with a six-month history of intermittent chest pain, two months following her prior evaluation for bilateral knee osteoarthritis, with known history of obesity, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, and gastroesophageal reflux disease.
The pain is described as a burning sensation located retrosternally, which often occurs after meals and lasts for several hours.
She denies any exertional component to the pain.
She also reports a sensation of food sticking in her chest and frequent heartburn, especially when lying down.
She has tried over-the-counter antacids with partial relief of her symptoms.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1.5 packs per day for 23 years (34.5 pack-years), with intermittent periods of reduced consumption.
She denies cough, wheezing, or shortness of breath.
Her vital signs are within normal limits
An electrocardiogram shows normal sinus rhythm with no ischemic changes.
Upper endoscopy reveals mild erythema of the distal esophagus, but no ulcers or masses.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of pain and swelling over the upper medial aspect of her right tibia that worsens with jogging and improves with rest; recently increased running distance for half marathon training.

lines: Two-month history of pain and swelling over the upper medial aspect of her right tibia that worsens with jogging and improves with rest; recently increased running distance for half marathon training.
The patient returns with a new complaint, evaluated in January 2020 for knee pain.
She reports that the pain worsens with activity, especially after jogging, and improves with rest.
She has recently increased her running distance in preparation for a half marathon.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
She has a history of osteoarthritis.
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1.5 packs per day for 23 years (34.5 pack-years), with intermittent periods of reduced consumption.
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the medial knee, just below the joint line.
There is no erythema or warmth, but a small, nonfluctuant swelling is noted.
Knee range of motion is full, but pain is elicited with resisted knee flexion.
Radiographs of the knee show no fractures or significant joint space narrowing.

encounters.cc: Desires contraceptive counseling specifically regarding initiating the contraceptive patch; has regular monthly periods and is not currently using birth control.

lines: Desires contraceptive counseling specifically regarding initiating the contraceptive patch; has regular monthly periods and is not currently using birth control.
The patient is a 44-year-old female with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Obesity presenting for gynecologic consultation following recent orthopedic care.
She has regular monthly periods and is not currently on any birth control.
She recently attended a bachelorette party where several of her friends were discussing how easy and effective the contraceptive patch is, and now she is interested in starting it.
She wants something that doesn't require daily attention and expresses concern about gaining weight with injectable contraception.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
She is in a monogamous relationship and would prefer not to use condoms.
However, she has smoked approximately 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day since the age of 20.
She reports that her job in event coordination is highly stressful and that she often smokes more when under pressure.
On examination, her blood pressure is 124/82 mm Hg, pulse is 74/min, and BMI is 25.
She has no signs of hirsutism, acne, or other hyperandrogenic features.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of a bulge in her right groin that gradually increases in size, more prominent with coughing or standing and reduces when lying down; denies associated pain.

lines: Three-month history of a bulge in her right groin that gradually increases in size, more prominent with coughing or standing and reduces when lying down; denies associated pain.
This 44-year-old female with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis presents with a groin bulge.
She reports that the bulge becomes more prominent when she coughs or stands for long periods and reduces in size when she lies down.
She denies any pain associated with the bulge.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
Her past medical history is significant for obesity and hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled.
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1.5 packs per day for 23 years (34.5 pack-years), with intermittent periods of reduced consumption.
The patient's vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, a non-tender, non-pulsatile mass is palpated below the inguinal ligament on the right side.
Valsalva maneuver increases the size of the mass.
No bowel sounds are heard over the mass.

encounters.cc: Intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to her back for 6 months; describes pain as crampy and occasionally associated with meals.

lines: Intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to her back for 6 months; describes pain as crampy and occasionally associated with meals.

This 45-year-old female with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, and prior gastroenterology evaluation for GERD presents with a 6-month history of intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain that radiates to her back.
She describes the pain as crampy and occasionally associated with meals.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
Her past medical history is significant for gastroesophageal reflux disease.
She underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 18 months ago.
Smoking: Current smoker, 1.5 packs per day for 23 years (34.5 pack-years), with intermittent periods of reduced consumption.
Vital signs are within normal limits
Abdominal examination reveals mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Laboratory tests show normal liver function tests and lipase.
An abdominal ultrasound reveals no gallstones or biliary ductal dilatation.

encounters.cc: Worsening difficulty swallowing over the past 6 months affecting both solids and liquids with nocturnal regurgitation of undigested food; unintentional weight loss of 4.5 kg.

lines: Worsening difficulty swallowing over the past 6 months affecting both solids and liquids with nocturnal regurgitation of undigested food; unintentional weight loss of 4.5 kg.
The patient, a 46-year-old female with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and history of postcholecystectomy syndrome, returns with symptoms.
She reports difficulty with both solids and liquids and often regurgitates undigested food, especially at night.
She has unintentionally lost 4.5 kg (10 lb) over the past several months.
She has no history of heartburn, choking, or coughing spells.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 10 years.

encounters.cc: Severe epigastric pain radiating to her back with nausea and vomiting for 24 hours; pain is constant and worsens after eating.

lines: Severe epigastric pain radiating to her back with nausea and vomiting for 24 hours; pain is constant and worsens after eating.

This 46-year-old female with obesity, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, and prior postcholecystectomy syndrome presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of severe epigastric pain radiating to her back, nausea, and vomiting.
She reports that the pain is constant and worsens after eating.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, diagnosed 2 years prior)
She has a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity.
- Right femoral hernia repair with mesh (recent)
She denies alcohol use but mentions that her diet is high in fats and carbohydrates.
On physical examination, her temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and heart rate is 102 beats per minute.
Abdominal examination reveals epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding.
There is no jaundice or scleral icterus.
A skin examination shows multiple, small, yellowish papules over the extensor surfaces of her arms and legs.
